_doc.training_engine: List of TrainsPotWorkChain.training_engine values (MACE/META/NEQUIP) whose postprocess step can produce this pair_style.
_doc.base_pair_style: LAMMPS pair_style string. Also used, unchanged, as the hybrid/overlay sub-style (with its own args) when combined with the vdw_d2 protocol, and as the key looked up in aiida-lammps' own lammps_potentials.json to find the potential's filename.
_doc.pair_coeff: Which token recipe (see _PAIR_COEFF_TOKENS in potential_engines.py: filename_symbols / symbols / atomic_numbers) builds the 'pair_coeff * * ...' line. Omit entirely if aiida-lammps' own read_from_file default already handles it.
_doc.style_options: Optional format string (with a {filename} placeholder) for potential_style_options, the extra text placed on the pair_style line itself. Omit if this pair_style needs none.
_doc._ordering: For a training_engine compatible with more than one entry (e.g. mliap), the FIRST matching entry in this file is used as its default -- put an engine's own native format before any extra format it can also export.

metatomic._comment: style_options is just the filename -- LAMMPS syntax is 'pair_style metatomic <file>'.

allegro._comment: Same training_engine as nequip: aiida-trainspot doesn't distinguish an 'ALLEGRO' training_engine, both come from the nequip.base training workflow.

mliap._comment: An extra export format, not any engine's native one -- listed after mace/nequip/allegro so it's never picked as their default. Unlike the other engines, the potential file is referenced via style_options ('unified <file> 0' on the pair_style line), not in pair_coeff, hence 'symbols' with no filename token there.
